According to recent reports, greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

According to recent reports, of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

In a recent development, elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

It has been revealed that mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Meanwhile, the big news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

He was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

In a recent development, I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

For further reading, check out my weekly column in which I look at three ways in which Arsenal have evolved this season.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026.

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways….

Sources indicate that it would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain.

It has been revealed that and what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

Industry observers note that we can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

Sources indicate that white's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back.

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel mentioned on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Industry observers note that jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Industry observers note that trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred.

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion.

It has been revealed that no goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

In a recent development, his swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men.

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his massive ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Substantial Red that night.

Sources indicate that my phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“We have the results of your biopsy.”.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”.

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”.

Sources indicate that as of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a initiative for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very massive way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

It has been revealed that which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

Sources indicate that so, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most important thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Industry observers note that some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

It has been revealed that I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

It has been revealed that I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

Industry observers note that I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

According to recent reports, so that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

DeepMind’s ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2024, researchers found a upcoming driver of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD): it was a gene called ETS2 that is overactive in immune cells owing to a DNA variant that predisposes people to the condition1.
  • Industry observers note that that discovery had involved gene-editing and other sophisticated molecular-biology techniques, and it identified potential fresh IBD treatments.
  • Sources indicate that “They’ve managed to figure out the answer in 30 minutes, and it took us a year and a half of experiments,” states James Lee, an immunologist and geneticist at the Francis Crick Institute in London, who led the 2024 study.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2024, researchers found a upcoming driver of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD): it was a gene called ETS2 that is overactive in immune cells owing to a DNA variant that predisposes people to the condition1. This variant had previously confounded researchers because it lies in a ‘gene desert’ nowhere near protein-coding sequences.

Industry observers note that that discovery had involved gene-editing and other sophisticated molecular-biology techniques, and it identified potential fresh IBD treatments. Now, researchers at Google DeepMind in London have replicated aspects of the finding using an artificial-intelligence model, and they have done this without lifting a pipette. Their model is called AlphaGenome 2.

Sources indicate that “They’ve managed to figure out the answer in 30 minutes, and it took us a year and a half of experiments,” states James Lee, an immunologist and geneticist at the Francis Crick Institute in London, who led the 2024 study. “It’s reassuring from our perspective.”.

According to recent reports, the AlphaGenome 2 model, which was declared today, is an update to an AI tool that predicts the molecular effects that ‘non-coding’ DNA sequences have, such as on the expression of other genes. These sequences comprise 98% of the human genome, but they are among the hardest to decipher. The latest model makes these predictions in hundreds of mouse and human cell types.

Two months ago, Google DeepMind released the AlphaGenome Atlas: these were predictions for every possible single-letter DNA change to the human genome — a total of nine billion variants.

These and other predictions were made with a tool called AlphaGenome 1 and came with a major caveat: they did not specify the precise kind of cell — be it antibody-making B cells or pancreatic β-cells — in which a variant was likely to act. “Having something that cannot predict cell-type specificity is a bit of a problem, which is why it hasn’t been hugely useful for us,” notes Lee.

But researchers know that many non-coding DNA sequences — including the variant that Lee’s team mapped, which is part of a sequence called a gene enhancer — tend to be active in specific types of cell.

“If you want to understand variants associated with genetic diseases, then you have to ask yourself what are the cell types that are affected,” says Žiga Avsec, a DeepMind researcher who leads the AlphaGenome team.

To develop an AI model that could decipher variant effects in diverse cells, Avsec’s team trained AlphaGenome 2 on single-cell gene activity and other measurements made in more than 100 million cells, across 68 tissues. AlphaGenome 1, by contrast, was fed data collected in ‘bulk’ samples of heterogeneous cells.

The result is a richer, more fine-grained representation of the differences between cells, says Adam Gayoso, a Google DeepMind scientist and co-author of a preprint describing the model on the organization’s website.

Industry observers note that alphaGenome 2 also isn’t limited to making predictions in the 637 types of human cell and 311 kinds of mouse cell it was trained on. Researchers can provide the model with new single-cell gene-activity data — such as those from cells in a disease state — and generate gene-variant predictions. This could help researchers to identify variants underlying disease more promptly, says Gayoso.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03673-0.

By Ben Sully | 16 Nov 2026 23:52, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 04:08.

Arsenal have reportedly reached an agreement with Declan Rice over a new long-term contract.

Rice is right now on the deal he signed when he arrived from West Ham in a £105m transfer in the summer of 2023.

That contract runs until June 2028, with an option to extend by a further 12 months, but his current terms are set to be replaced by a latest deal.

The England international recently gave an patch on his Arsenal future, revealing that a fresh deal will "hopefully be arriving soon".

As per The Athletic, Rice has now agreed a upcoming five-year contract that will see him extend his Arsenal stay into the next decade, with an official confirmation expected in the near future.

The latest contract will keep him at the Emirates Stadium for his peak years, given he will be 32 by the time the proposed deal expires in 2031.

The report suggests the terms of the deal will reflect Rice's status as an integral member of the Arsenal squad.

The 27-year-old has made 173 competitive appearances for the Gunners, contributing 22 goals and 36 assists.

Rice started 35 of his 36 league appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, as he played a key role in ending Arsenal's 22-year wait for Premier League glory.

The Englishman is not the only player who is set to sign fresh terms, with The Athletic reporting that Timber has agreed to a contract extension with the Gunners.

Timber's proposed newly introduced contract will see him extend his stay beyond the end of his current deal, which expires in the summer of 2028.

Ismaelo Ganiou has been one of the most promising young defenders in France since he broke into Lens' team last season.

Ganiou would be a smart addition for Liverpool, who would be looking to recreate the success they found in signing Jeremy Jacquet from Ligue 1, but only time will tell whether the 21-year-old ends up at Anfield.

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Sources indicate that milan debuted the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Sources indicate that under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Recent findings suggest that asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

According to recent reports, similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Recent findings suggest that milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

According to recent reports, milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most key aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

According to recent reports, rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

According to recent reports, perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 05:14.

Gremio will host Bahia at their Arena do Gremio home in Porto Alegre on Wednesday night, for a crucial showdown that will have ramifications for both the Brasileirao's relegation battle and race for Copa Libertadores qualification.

The Tricolor dos Pampas are hoping to build on their cup success last time out, while the Steel Squad are keen to bounce back from defeat.

Renato Portaluppi's Gremio have endured a dire league campaign so far, but they are far from doomed in the Brazilian top flight.

The Tricolor dos Pampas held Athletico Mineiro to a 1-1 draw in the second leg of their Copa do Brasil semi-final on November 7, earning a 3-1 aggregate victory and a place in the final against Palmeiras.

In the Brasileirao, Portaluppi's side are at the moment 18th with 37 points to their name, sitting in the relegation zone with just four games to play.

However, Gremio are only one point shy of 16th-placed Internacional and 15th-placed Vitoria, giving the team genuine hope as the season enters its final stretch.

This week's hosts will also be buoyed by the fact they have lost just one of their last four home matches across all competitions, beating Mineiro 2-0 in the first leg of their cup tie after another 2-0 triumph over Athletico Paranaense in the league.

Meanwhile, Rogerio Ceni's Bahia are pushing for a place in the Copa Libertadores next term, and are currently in position to make the qualifiers, though the pressure is mounting.

The Steel Squad are sixth with 53 points, and with four matches remaining on their calendar, they sit one point short of fifth-placed Athletico Paranaense, and four behind fourth-placed Fluminense, who occupy one of the automatic entry spots.

That being stated, Bahia's ambitions took a hit last time out on November 6, when they were downed 3-2 by Cruzeiro, who came from behind to win on a disappointing evening in Belo Horizonte.

As a result, Ceni's men are now within reach of seventh-placed Mineiro, who are a mere two points back in seventh after their goalless draw with Mirassol on Saturday.

To make matters worse, the visitors come into this clash having lost three of their past four away games, drawing once - a 1-1 stalemate with Santos late last month.

On the other hand, Bahia have played one match fewer than Mineiro, and Wednesday night represents a chance for them to strengthen their cushion over their rivals in the race for Libertadores qualification.

Gremio form (all competitions):.

Gremio are without midfielders Mathias Villasanti (suspended), Juan Nardoni (thigh) and Danilo (muscle), though Dodi and Filip Krovinovic should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Walter Kannemann is also suspended for accumulating yellow cards, while right-back options Diego Caito and Cristian Pavon are sidelined due to respective muscle injuries.

In their absence, Gustavo Martins, Wallace and Fabian Balbuena look set to start in a three-man defence, flanked by wing-backs Joao Pedro and Marlon.

As for Bahia, they are missing goalkeeper Leo Vieira, who is out for the season with a knee injury, while centre-half Marco Moreno is a doubt with stomach trouble.

If the latter is unavailable, then David Duarte and Kanu should be ready to start in front of shot-stopper Ronaldo.

Gremio possible starting lineup:.

Weverton; Martins, Wallace, Balbuena; Pedro, Dodi, Krovinovic, Marlon; Enamorado, Vinicius, Amuzu.

Bahia possible starting lineup:.

Ronaldo; Victor, Duarte, Kanu, Juba; Erick, Acevedo, Nestor; Oliveira, Veliz, Pulga.

Gremio may be in the relegation zone, but they arrive in better form than their opponents and will be optimistic about delivering a strong performance.

However, Bahia will be motivated by the race for Libertadores action, and are unlikely to be beaten again after their frustrating defeat last time out.

It’ll be Ben White on the night

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (844 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid.
  • According to recent reports, obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England.
  • Holland was the one who sparked the glitch originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid. Ezri Konsa made it 2-0 with a close range header, Spain might wonder who was marking him (I think it was supposed to be Marc Cucurella) but the movement was really sharp. Then a couple of minute later, Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead, with Cucurella also in close attendance.

According to recent reports, obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England. The worst sections of the media have fanned the flames against him, and it doesn’t take much to rile up those who are already of a jingoistic persuasion. As we’ve seen since seen with stories about Steve Holland being hugely unpopular at Man Utd, there’s a common denominator, and it’s not Ben White.

Holland was the one who sparked the glitch originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick. I also feel quite confident that even if there is a cohort who won’t forgive Ben White for the crime of Steve Holland being a dickhead, he probably won’t care too much. Look at the reactions of his teammates and manager to the goal, and that’s tells you plenty.

He was also involved in a minor scuffle going off at half-time, which also seemed to involved Konsa and Martin Zubimendi, but I’m sure it was just heat of the moment stuff. Although Spain got two back after England went down to 10 men, they made the fatal mistake of starting Mikel Merino. How was he supposed to come off the bench and get a vital goal then? Silly Luis de la Fuenta, bloke’s a fraud.

In a recent development, elsewhere over the weekend, Viktor Gyokeres scored twice for Sweden, both from the penalty spot. We just need more penalties. This is the key to unlocking him. Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 as Italy went down 4-1 to Belgium (ouch), Martin Odegaard played 90 as Norway beat Wales, and there are some more games to come this week with Germany facing Netherlands tonight (Kai v Timber), the Brazilians are in action in Singapore, and apparently Christos Tzolis is fit to play for Greece after having an MRI.

Maybe it’s my own recent experiences, but I don’t care for the idea he needs an MRI. I get it, it’s probably for his knee or hamstring or something, but it feels like if you need one of those to know if you’re fit, you’re probably not feeling 100% anyway. I guess this will be one Mikel Arteta will keep a close eye on tonight when Greece host Serbia and Tzolis inevitably starts. Ideally, these will be useful minutes for him, and help him deliver for us but you can’t help but worry considering he picked up an injury in the last Interlull.

Recent findings suggest that finally for today, it looks as if a Declan Rice contract extension is close. Speaking while on England duty, he mentioned:.

“A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon. I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy and effort into to me.

“I’m extremely lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, and it makes playing football far more easier.”.

This is, by any measure, a no-brainer. I don’t think there’s a club in the world that would turn him down if he were available, and his importance to Arsenal is just obvious. In a world when £100m+ transfers often struggle to provide value, this is one of the exceptions. If you went back to 2023 and had to do it all again, even if you added another £20m or £30m to the fee we paid West Ham, it would be worth it. It’s likely to be the kind of deal that sees him play out the rest of his prime years in red and white, and let’s hope there are more trophies along the way to accompany that.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

Recent findings suggest that the pod should be out around around midday. Until then, have a good one – after which I’m gonna be off for a couple of days but the lads will keep things ticking here until I get back.

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 00:33.

Hungary boss Marco Rossi has insisted Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai is fit to play in Tuesday's UEFA Nations League clash against Northern Ireland.

Szoboszlai was forced off with a minor knee issue in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

As a result, there was some doubt as to whether he would link up with the Hungary squad for the final two matches of the Nations League league phase.

Not only did he join up with his national team, but he played the full duration of Saturday's 2-0 away win over Georgia, in which he provided an assist for Barnabas Varga's 85th-minute effort.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he was close to pulling out of the game after feeling the injury in the pre-match warm-up.

The midfielder also said his leg "felt good" during the game and that he would start the "treatment process all over again" in a bid to be ready for Tuesday's home meeting with Northern Ireland.

Speaking in Monday's pre-match press conference, Rossi attempted to ease fears over Szoboszlai's injury status, insisting his captain is ready to feature at the Puskas Arena.

Industry observers note that “Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?” Rossi noted.

“I didn’t see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

Industry observers note that “I don’t think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don’t think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia.”.

For Hungary, Tuesday's game is an vital fixture as it offers the chance to secure promotion to League A of the Nations League.

Having collected 10 points from their five matches, Hungary enter the final matchday in second spot and one point behind leaders Northern Ireland in Group B2.

Meanwhile, Liverpool's main priority is Sunday's Premier League clash against Manchester United, who will start life under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will be keen to have Szoboszlai available for the home fixture, especially as there is doubt over Ryan Gravenberch's availability.

Divine Dowman does it again

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again.
  • In a recent development, I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week.
  • Industry observers note that it’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again. I suppose after 24 years of writing this blog, a few bad habits are bound to creep in….

In a recent development, I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week. Fortunately, a lifetime of watching Arsenal has given me plenty of practice at making bad jokes when I don’t know what else to say.

Industry observers note that it’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend. Bluesky, Reddit, X, Discord, Facebook, Patreon. Wherever I looked, there you were, sending love to Blogs. It was beautiful to see.

And to the handful of you who got in touch with me or people I know because you thought Friday’s revision was about my health, please hold that thought. I’m fine. Touch wood. There are, in fact, two Andrews at Arseblog, and I’m the other one.

Having been crowned the “World’s Youngest Boy” by James on yesterday’s Arsecast Extra, Max Dowman set yet another record last night, becoming England under-21s’ youngest scorer with the winner in a 3-2 victory over France in filthy conditions in Bristol.

I’d planned to watch from kick-off, but gave up when I realised the game wasn’t on any of the 5,000 channels I pay £150 a month for. Then I saw on social media that Ethan Nwaneri, playing as a number 10, had laid on a couple of goals. So I did the clever thing and googled it. Turns out I needed the official England app and an account. Eyes still rolling, I tried to set up a login, only to find out I already had one. Cue the password reset process, verification codes and me losing the will to live. Just let me watch some fucking children play football in the rain!

By the time I got the stream, it was nearly half-time. At least that gave me a chance to catch up on Nwaneri’s two assists, both of which were Ozil-esque. First he drove down the left and slipped a neat ball inside for Mikey Moore, at the moment on loan at Cologne, to finish. Then came a teasing dink to the back post that Southampton’s Divin Mubama met first time. Given how little Nwaneri has played for Dortmund lately, it was a welcome reminder of what he can do.

It feels a bit silly to say Max, who was named player of the match, looked comfortable at this level when he’s already got a Premier League winners’ medal next to his GCSE textbooks, but he really did.

Watching him is like reading someone’s really nice handwriting. Even the everyday stuff looks lovely. A touch to bring the ball under control, a little turn, and suddenly the defender who was right up his arse is looking at the back of his shirt. I’ll never get tired of watching him do that.

As both sides made changes, I expected Lee Carsley to take him off. Instead, he played the full 90 and dug Arsenal teammate Tommy Setford out of a hole. The goalkeeper was at fault for the only goal in Friday’s defeat to Portugal and had another difficult night, spilling a cross into his own net. The rain hardly helped, and the 20-year-old has been doing well on loan at Stevenage, but it was a horrible one to concede.

When Brest’s Giovani Versini whipped in an equaliser with five minutes left, it looked like England would have to settle for a draw, but Dowman’s tap-in settled it with a minute to spare. Who knows, Dowman and Nwaneri could be on the same pitch again next week when Dortmund visit the Emirates.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, Group 2 of League A of the UEFA Nations League (catchy naming scheme, lads) served up another bonkers evening. Jurrien Timber scored twice in the Netherlands’ 7-0 win over Christos Tzolis’ Greece on Friday, only for the Dutch to lose 5-0 to Kai Havertz’s Germany in Berlin. There were some lovely goals from the Germans – including two from Florian Wirtz – who are finding their feet under Jurgen Klopp. Timber and Havertz both came off midway through the second half, seemingly unscathed. Timber’s pride aside, anyway.

Tzolis, meanwhile, was cleared to play after an MRI scan and got through 88 minutes of Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia. All three sides finished on 11 points, with Germany and the Netherlands going through on goal difference at Greece’s expense.

Tonight, Martin Odegaard’s Norway face Denmark, while Viktor Gyokeres will look to extend his record-breaking scoring run for Sweden away at Poland. Piero Hincapie’s Ecuador take on Bolivia, Big Gabi and Bruno are in Singapore with Brazil, and Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon are in action for Spain under-21s and England under-19s, respectively.

In a recent development, closer to home, The Athletic ran two Arsenal contract stories in quick succession. James reports that Timber has agreed a newly introduced long-term deal, while David Ornstein says Declan Rice’s extension will take him through to 2031. Arsenal already had the option to keep Rice until 2029, so the new deal effectively buys them two more years and gives him a sizeable pay rise for the next four and a half. If he keeps playing as he has been, I can’t imagine many Arsenal fans quibbling with that.

For what it’s worth, we’ve heard on the grapevine that David Raya’s latest contract is all but done, too, which means the club are making good progress with the lads whose deals expire in 2028, a list that also includes Odegaard, Havertz, Mikel Merino and our two backup keepers.

There was an interesting discussion on Arsenal Vision’s ‘Friday Night Clive’ podcast about Arsenal elongating their “winning window” while having one eye on the next iteration of the team. If you hand expensive new contracts to players hurtling towards their thirties, you leave yourself financially exposed and potentially blocking pathways for up-and-coming talent. No doubt the club and manager are keenly aware of that. I just wonder how much you can expect the latter to focus on the faraway future when the dynasty he craves has to start in the here and now.

If this week has taught me anything, it’s that there’s something to be stated for seizing the day. Admittedly, that’s easier when it’s Arsenal’s money I’m volunteering to spend.

If you’re about to part with some of your own (smooth segue, Allen) this year’s Arseblog Christmas Gift Guide is up.

I spent some of last week rounding up Arsenal bits and pieces I’d be happy to find under the tree. Mostly, I wanted to point you towards the independent makers, artists and writers producing stuff I like. In many cases, what I’ve picked is just a small sample of what they do, so have a nose around.

If you’ve got a recommendation of your own, pop the link in the form at the bottom and I’ll take a look.

Sources indicate that right, I’d better crack on with the day job. Lewis is on duty tomorrow and, all being well, Andrew M should be back here before the week is out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

According to recent reports, immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

In a recent development, he has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Industry observers note that moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby reveals, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

It has been revealed that he set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is right now captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

In a recent development, amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

According to recent reports, the leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

Iraola's side find themselves fourth in the league, but already nine points shy of first after 10 matches.

It is becoming clear that there is still work to be done on the squad, and the Anfield recruitment team are hard at work trying to identify the right deals for the upcoming winter window.

Several exciting names have been linked, but the Reds have now reportedly joined the race for another.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool to battle Premier League rivals for Bundesliga starBilal El Khannouss has proven himself as one of the best young talents in the Bundesliga since his move from Leicester at the start of last season. Bilal El Khannouss has proven himself as one of the best young talents in the Bundesliga since his move from Leicester at the start of last season.

The 47-capped Morocco international can play on either wing but is primarily used as an attacking midfielder, and has become a key part of Stuttgart's attacking unit.

The 22-year-old has had a fairly slow start to this campaign, scoring twice in 15 appearances, 10 of which were starts.

El Khannouss' talent is clear to see though, and the dynamic attacker produced 16 goals and assists for Stuttgart last season, also providing two assists for Leicester before his move.

The Moroccan was heavily linked with a switch to Brighton in the summer, but the deal ultimately fell through, and now several Premier League clubs are interested.

That's according to Ekrem Konur, who has revealed Liverpool alongside Leeds and Newcastle are chasing a deal for El Khannouss, with Galatasaray also closely monitoring the situation.

Liverpool are presently well-stocked for wide options but lack a true alternative to Florian Wirtz in the number 10 role, a gap that El Khannouss could easily fill for the Reds.

Konur doesn't reveal a potential fee, but with interest so high a bidding war could ensue, driving the 22-year-old's price higher.

Khannouss would be a sensible addition for the Reds and is definitely a player to keep an eye on heading into the winter window.

  • Arsenal youngster Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goalscorer in Monday's 3-2 win over France.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 04:00.

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goalscorer in Monday's 3-2 win over France.

After making 13 appearances for England's Under-19 side, Dowman earned his first call-up to the Under-21 squad for the current international window.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player to represent England Under-21s when he featured as a substitute in the 1-0 defeat against Portugal in Friday's friendly at Ashton Gate, surpassing the record previously held by Jude Bellingham.

Dowman was then given the chance to start Monday's friendly against France, and he made the most of his opportunity, scoring an 89th-minute winner after England had spurned a two-goal lead.

Recent findings suggest that the winning goal ✨ Max Dowman has his first goal for our #YoungLions! https://t.co/gb4rLaXXBV.

Everton's Harrison Armstrong created the winner, stealing possession high up the pitch before squaring the ball for Dowman to steer home a simple left-foot finish.

As a result of the effort, Dowman took another record away from Bellingham as he became England Under-21s' youngest-ever scorer.

Dowman found the net at the age of 16 years and 320 days old, surpassing the record Bellingham set when he scored on his Under-21s debut against Kosovo at the age of 17 years and 67 days in September 2020.

The Arsenal academy product also picked up the Player of the Match award as he helped Carsley's side end a three-game winless run.

In a recent development, the winning goal and your #YoungLions Player of the Match connected by @EE! ? Max Dowman ? https://t.co/eNmPkLLWVN.

In regard to the England Under-21s, Dowman will hope to be part of the squad that heads to Albania and Serbia next summer for the European Under-21 Championship.

In the short term, the winger will link back up with his Arsenal teammates, who will prepare for Saturday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle United.

However, he will be unable to feature against the Magpies as he serves the final match of the three-game ban he received following his red card in the EFL Cup defeat against Fleetwood Town.

Dowman could return to the squad for the Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund on November 24, just days before the Gunners take on Manchester City in the Premier League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

It has been revealed that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

In a recent development, for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

According to recent reports, keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews remarked. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

It has been revealed that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

It has been revealed that to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

Industry observers note that it was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak stated. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Industry observers note that any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

Recent findings suggest that the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” remarked Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa remarked: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

According to recent reports, 9 - Florian Wirtz's nine chances created from open play against Brentford is the most by a player in a Premier League game since Sadio Mané v Burnley in January 2021 (9) and the most by a player in an away game since Samir Nasri v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Liverpool have two deals in place already. We believe both should be completed ASAP.

In a recent development, liverpool must sort their defensive situation out as it's one that risks getting massively out of hand. And that'll take some work.

As things stand, there are only two centre-backs in the first-team squad who are contracted to the club beyond this season. One is Jeremy Jacquet and the other Giovanni Leoni.

Sources indicate that only one of those has actually finished 90 minutes for Liverpool. It is, in other words, a less-than-ideal situation and one which will give Julian Ward and organization a real headache.

Virgil van Dijk is out of contract, of course, as is Joe Gomez. Ronald Araujo's loan will end, too, and that trims the squad down dramatically. Fortunately, there's a relatively easy way to fix things as Liverpool do have two centre-backs deals lined up and agreed.

They just need to trigger them.

Liverpool's centre-back double-dealsAraujo, of course, may not leave. Liverpool have the option to sign the defender for €55m from Barcelona as long as he wants to commit to the Reds. Marca is among those claiming he wants to do just that, even if Liverpool need to wait until the end of the season to actually trigger the option. It appears, though, that the club are in favour of signing Araujo and that he will be a centre-back option beyond this season.

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:48.

The final playoff game on the Western Conference side will take place Thursday as the Seattle Sounders host Real Salt Lake in the MLS Wild Card Round at Lumen Field.

These teams wound up eighth and ninth in the West during the regular season, with the Rave Green defeating Los Angeles FC the last time out 2-1, putting them a point above Salt Lake, who won by that same score on Decision Day against the Los Angeles Galaxy.

It was an underwhelming regular season overall for Seattle, but they managed to get a result when needed to keep their campaign alive.

While they finished with nine fewer points this year than in 2025, Brian Schmetzer’s men found a way to stay above the playoff line by the skin of their teeth.

They have dropped points in five of their last six games but have won more playoff encounters than any MLS club (26) since their debut season in the league in 2009.

In 2026, the Sounders lost four more home games (five) than the year before, though they have only lost one playoff match at Lumen Field this decade in normal time, with Los Angeles FC blanking them 1-0 in 2023.

This will be the first time they compete in the Wild Card Round, with the Rave Green winning their first post-season home outing in 2025.

The Sounders are unbeaten in their last four MLS home games versus Real Salt Lake, collecting a clean sheet on three of those occasions.

Like Seattle, Salt Lake came up massive when needed on Decision Day, qualifying for the post-season for a sixth consecutive time.

While Pablo Mastroeni has never missed the playoffs since taking charge of this team in 2021, they lost their only Wild Card outing last year at the Portland Timbers (3-1).

On Thursday, RSL will try to end a four-match playoff losing run and win their first post-season game away from home since upsetting Sporting Kansas City 2-1 in 2021.

During the 2026 MLS campaign, Claret and Cobalt were pointless in their three away outings against the Cascadia clubs (the Portland Timbers, Vancouver Whitecaps and Sounders), netting just one goal overall against those teams.

Entering this must-win game, however, the club from Sandy, Utah have won two of their last three MLS away encounters.

Their recent playoff form may not be great, but RSL have won their last two knockout matches against Seattle across all competitions, upsetting them on penalties at Lumen Field in the opening round of the 2021 MLS Cup playoffs.

Seattle Sounders Major League Soccer form:.

Real Salt Lake Major League Soccer form:.

Both Alex Roldan and Danny Musovski will be questionable for the Sounders on Thursday, with the former recovering from a calf strain and the latter from a head injury.

A knee problem will likely keep Nikola Petkovic out as well, while Yeimar Gomez Andrade has a sore hamstring and Pedro de la Vega is doubtful with a quad matter.

Albert Rusnak and Sebastian Gomez netted first-half goals which were ultimately just enough to earn them a win against LAFC.

As for Real Salt Lake, Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are both unlikely to feature in this upcoming fixture due to knee injuries.

There were several newly introduced faces in their starting 11 on Decision Day, with Kobi Henry and Zach Booth among those being inserted on the backline.

Sergi Solans and Booth found the back of the net early versus the Galaxy, while an own goal from Luc de Fougerolles led to some anxious moments in the second half before the final whistle blew.

Thomas; Kossa-Rienzi, Kee-hee, Ragen, Tolo; Dotson, C. Roldan; Morris, Rusnak, Ferreira; Joveljic.

Real Salt Lake possible starting lineup:.

Cabral; Sanabria, Glad, De Fougerolles, Quinton, Booth; Guilavogui, Caliskan, Spierings, Lobjanhidze; Solans.

Scientists’ knowledge of the connectivity, robustness and functionality of complex networks — such as those that describe interactions in chemical and biological systems, social relationships and the Internet — has increased enormously over the past few decades1. The foundations of modern complex-network science were established by the pioneering contributions of Albert-László Barabási and Réka Albert2,3, who revealed universal mechanisms that explain the emergence of highly non-uniform network configurations. Writing in Nature, Both et al.4 report that ideas from network science can be used to design materials that have remarkable mechanical properties, incorporating connection diversity and variable component sizes found in complex systems into materials engineering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:52.

With a spot in the opening phase of the MLS Cup playoffs up for grabs, Orlando City will welcome FC Cincinnati to Inter.com Stadium in the Sunshine State on Thursday for that Wild Card matchup.

The Lions finished the regular season eighth, blanking the Latest England Revolution 1-0 in their last meeting, with Cincy below them after a 2-0 Decision Day home defeat to Nashville SC.

A season that appeared headed for disaster in the spring came to life in the late summer as Orlando City recovered and climbed back above the playoff line.

The arrival of Antoine Griezmann changed their fortunes dramatically, with nine of this club’s 13 wins coming after the 2018 World Cup winner arrived.

Martin Perelman’s men are unbeaten in their last seven MLS outings at home, dropping points on only one of those occasions.

On Thursday they can collect their first post-season triumph since the 2024 Eastern Conference semi-finals when they blanked Atlanta United 1-0.

Orlando have won six straight league contests at home when netting the opening goal and have never lost a playoff game on home soil when doing so.

Thanks in part to Griezmann’s presence, the Lions rose to eighth in the league regarding average goals per game (1.9) in 2026.

In a win-and-in scenario on Decision Day, Cincinnati failed to deliver, ending a four-match domestic unbeaten run and setting up this Wild Card showdown.

A defeat on Thursday would mark the first time that the Orange and Blue fail to feature in the first round of the playoffs since Pat Noonan took charge ahead of the 2022 campaign.

Cincinnati have points in three successive MLS away encounters and have lost just one of their last five games domestically as the visitors.

They have never won a post-season away game in 90 minutes, with their only such triumph occurring in Newly introduced Jersey in 2023 on penalties versus the New York Red Bulls.

They averaged the fourth-most goals per match in the league this past season (2.0) but conceded the third-most per game (2.2) just slightly fewer than Orlando City, who were second from the bottom in that department (2.3).

The Orange and Blue are unbeaten in their last four MLS meeting versus Orlando City, while Noonan has never lost a match against them at Inter.co Stadium.

Orlando City Major League Soccer form:.

FC Cincinnati Major League Soccer form:.

But the expectations of the 15-cap international for his future club could mean Paris disappear from the equation.

According to information shared by The Touchline, Paz has two demands for the rest of his career and his future club.

All the more so as the Spanish manager readily practises rotation, even if some players are obviously more regular starters than others.

Still young (22), Paz left Real Madrid in 2024 to make a name for himself in Italy and then in Europe with Como.

Very early on, then, the Argentine put playing time ahead of everything else: a move to Como could represent a sporting gamble, as the Italian club, although backed by a billionaire, had just been promoted to Serie A.

For the rest of his career, therefore, the playmaker intends to be attentive to his playing time, even if his talent, now recognised, naturally opens doors for him.

According to recent reports, but not necessarily those of PSG, where competition is fierce in attack and in midfield. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:25.
  • Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin in the final round of the Nations League group stage.
  • In a convincing performance, the four-time world champions produced their best football since the arrival of Jurgen Klopp, who took charge of the national team after the disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:25.

Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin in the final round of the Nations League group stage.

In a convincing performance, the four-time world champions produced their best football since the arrival of Jurgen Klopp, who took charge of the national team after the disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

With goals from Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, Brajan Gruda and Florian Wirtz, who scored twice, the Germans produced an impressive result against opponents who were also fighting for top spot in the group.

It has been revealed that the victory took on even greater importance because of the situation before the match. Germany began the round in third place in Group A2, level on points with Greece and behind the Dutch, and risked missing out on the quarter-finals. With the win, they reached 11 points, overtook their rivals on goal difference and finished the first phase at the top, securing a place among the best eight in the competition.

One of the stars of the night was Derry Scherhant. Klopp’s selection on the left of the attack scored his first goal for the senior Germany team.

According to recent reports, A native of Berlin, the 24-year-old winger, who plays for Freiburg, took the opportunity to make his mark in front of the crowd of his home city. His exuberant celebration after finding the top corner past Bart Verbruggen reflected the special significance of the moment in his international career.

The goal also rewarded the faith the manager has placed in the attacker. Scherhant was only making his fourth appearance for the national team and has earned his place amid the renewal carried out by Klopp since he took over.

The chance given to the Freiburg player is part of a strategy that seeks to widen the squad’s options, without restricting selections to the best-known names in German football. Against the Netherlands, the youngster delivered and demonstrated that he can be an interesting option in attack.

Industry observers note that another standout was Wirtz, who again highlighted how his talent can make a difference in a Germany shirt. The attacking midfielder scored twice in the second half and was decisive in turning a lead built before the break into a rout. His ability to find space, accelerate attacks and arrive in positions to shoot gave another dimension to the German attack.

The performance reinforces one of the main positive certainties of the early days of Klopp’s reign: Wirtz is capable of taking on the team’s technical leadership.

Sources indicate that as well as the brilliance of the number 17 and Scherhant’s first goal, the match also underlined the importance of the opportunities given to other young players. Gruda, who had already scored in the 3-1 win over Serbia, found the net again during this international break and has now scored two goals for the national team.

Left-back Philipp Treu was also among the starters, benefiting from the opening up of opportunities by the manager. These are names that help to give shape to a project still under construction and show that Klopp intends to increase competition in different positions.

Sources indicate that it was a well-played and competitive first half, with good link-up play and quick transitions. At home, Germany had more possession and went for a proactive game, with a high line and patience to find space.

In the 41st minute, they found it: Scherhant received the ball on the right, got past Denzel Dumfries and curled a lovely shot across goal into the top corner past Verbruggen.

Industry observers note that the Netherlands, for their part, took to the pitch practically already qualified. In their tactical approach in the first half, the Dutch opted for a more reactive game: either Xavi Hernandez’s team reached dangerous areas through counter-attacks, or they drew in the German press and built from the back, passing the ball patiently.

At the start of the second half, Germany needed only a few minutes to punish the visitors again. Fourteen minutes into the half, Wirtz began a move down the left, tried to play a one-two with Scherhant, but saw Dumfries step in front of him. The Liverpool midfielder then regained the ball, dribbled past the Dutch full-back and struck hard with his left foot from the edge of the area to make it 2-0.

According to recent reports, from there it became a stroll. The Netherlands clearly felt the blow, and the hosts took advantage to turn the win into a rout. Schlotterbeck, with a header, Wirtz, with another stunning goal, and Gruda gave the match its final numbers.

In a recent development, juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He stated his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He remarked the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

It has been revealed that clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It highlights how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

Industry observers note that the gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

In a recent development, napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first confirmed an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.
