📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet.
  • In the end it also points to another thing.
  • Industry observers note that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

Industry observers note that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

Industry observers note that “It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Sources indicate that ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Industry observers note that can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick noted this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

According to recent reports, having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

According to recent reports, bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1.

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Industry observers note that leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

Sources indicate that but after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm.

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” remarked the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

It has been revealed that “But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

Recent findings suggest that “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick mentioned he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

Industry observers note that martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

It has been revealed that the Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

In a recent development, “It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

According to recent reports, “It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he mentioned: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

It has been revealed that “We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

Industry observers note that “They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”.

Newcastle United 0 Aston Villa 1.

It’s all over at Elland Road, with Leeds and Man Utd playing out a competitive draw. Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez debuted an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

Industry observers note that the Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

In a recent development, unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

Recent findings suggest that weston McKennie has left the door open to joining Manchester United, days after his USA coach Mauricio Pochettino took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

The question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

Industry observers note that mcKennie called the speculation inevitable. He said many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

It has been revealed that pochettino was asked about the same subject. He said now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

Pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

Sources indicate that the comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s looks and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

It has been revealed that mcKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

It has been revealed that the club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

In a recent development, the timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is also missing. Captain Manuel Locatelli twisted his right knee in the game against Milan. He then underwent surgery in Lyon to repair the external meniscus. The club described the operation as successful, with his rehabilitation programme due to start the following day.

Recent findings suggest that losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 13, 2026.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He noted nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

Industry observers note that the next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

Even giant anteaters in remote Brazil have microplastics in their blood

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, giant anteaters traipsing across Brazil’s pristine wetlands and savannahs have ingested traces of plastic pollutants.
  • Some of Brazil’s wildlife have traces of plastic circulating in their blood — even if they live far from land used by humans, according to an analysis published on 11 November in Nature1.
  • Researchers measured the concentration of microplastics in the blood of 47 animals: 26 lowland tapirs (Tapirus terrestris) and 21 giant anteaters (Myrmecophaga tridactyla).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, giant anteaters traipsing across Brazil’s pristine wetlands and savannahs have ingested traces of plastic pollutants. Credit: Sylvain Cordier/Gamma-Rapho via Getty.

Some of Brazil’s wildlife have traces of plastic circulating in their blood — even if they live far from land used by humans, according to an analysis published on 11 November in Nature1.

Researchers measured the concentration of microplastics in the blood of 47 animals: 26 lowland tapirs (Tapirus terrestris) and 21 giant anteaters (Myrmecophaga tridactyla). The scientists found that, on average, the creatures carry similar levels of plastic as many humans — roughly 74 particles per millilitre of blood. The animals that lived closest to human infrastructure and waste-management facilities had the highest levels of microplastics in their blood.

According to recent reports, but even those living more than 100 kilometres from a waste sites and 65 kilometres from human infrastructure showed traces of the pollutants. This indicates that plastics can reach wildlife living far from where the pollution originates, states study co-author Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, a conservation scientist at the University of British Columbia’s Okanagan campus in Kelowna, Canada.

The findings are an important step to better understand how the particles impact wildlife, notes Sofia Ya-Hsuan Liou, a geochemist at the National Taiwan University in Taipei.

Sources indicate that microplastics are tiny particles (smaller than five millimetres across) with many different chemical compositions. They can travel through the environment in rainwater, rivers and the atmosphere. Although several studies have measured microplastics levels in wildlife, few have explored how the surrounding environment influences what animals ingest, states study co-author Michael Noonan, a quantitative ecologist at the University of British Columbia’s Okanagan campus.

To find out, Noonan, Ferraz and their colleagues collected and analysed blood samples from animals living across the Amazon rainforest, the Cerrado savannah and the huge and pristine Pantanal wetland between February 2021 and November 2022. The researchers also used GPS data to track the animals’ movements and their exposure to a human footprint.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03660-5.

Federico Chiesa’s future could bring him back to Italy after a stint at Liverpool that fell far short of expectations.

In three seasons with the Reds, the attacking winger has failed to regain the consistency and performance that made him a star with Fiorentina, Juventus, and the national team.

This situation, on the cusp of turning thirty, could push him to seek a latest opportunity to relaunch his career. The most likely option would be a loan deal on advantageous terms, a solution that would satisfy both Liverpool and the player.

The English club would have the opportunity to develop Chiesa, potentially increasing his attractiveness on the transfer market, while the striker could return to playing more regularly. Also in the background is his goal of joining the national team, which he has been absent from for over two years.

With Roberto Mancini as manager, a return to the Italian league could offer him a chance to reclaim the Azzurri jersey, provided he can demonstrate on the pitch that he has regained his peak condition.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the most interesting prospects for the former Juventus player’s future lie in Rome, where both clubs in the capital could be evaluating his potential arrival. On the Giallorossi front, Gian Piero Gasperini is seeking additional attacking options and would be interested in adding a player with Chiesa’s qualities, especially in a low-cost move. Much will depend, however, on the financial terms of the potential transfer and the player’s fitness.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio could also enter the race, considering the possibility of strengthening their attack with an experienced player. The competition between the two Roman clubs does not, however, rule out interest from other Italian clubs, especially if Liverpool decides to facilitate the winger’s departure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roma is looking to the Netherlands to find the attacking winger requested by Gian Piero Gasperini.

It has been revealed that at the top of the list of possible reinforcements is Ruben van Bommel, the 22-year-old striker for PSV Eindhoven and the Dutch national team. Journalist Piero Torri revealed the news this morning on Manà Manà Sport Roma.

The son of a talented player, he’s one of the players the Giallorossi are most confidently targeting to strengthen their attack.

Van Bommel perfectly fits the profile of the winger Gasperini is seeking: he plays primarily on the left flank, is right-footed, has an imposing build, stands nearly 1.90 meters tall, and combines speed, power, and the ability to beat his opponent. He loves to start wide and then cut inside to shoot, but he’s also capable of attacking deep.

He’s a player with particularly interesting characteristics for the Roma coach’s aggressive, vertical style of football.

Sources indicate that van Bommel is being supported by Team Raiola and has a contract with PSV until June 2030. The Dutch club invested around €16 million to acquire him from AZ and would be unlikely to let him leave on particularly favorable terms. This is an aspect that Roma will eventually have to evaluate, along with the deal’s formula and the financial margins for January’s move.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Real Madrid had a particularly eventful evening on the Valencia pitch.
  • It all started with the protests of Braulio Vázquez, Valencia’s sporting director, who was particularly upset with the refereeing, particularly after a foul preceding Madrid’s first goal.
  • And the accusations are particularly serious.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Real Madrid had a particularly eventful evening on the Valencia pitch. If the Merengues displayed their superiority on the field (3-0), the meeting was also marked by numerous tensions between the two teams. In a particularly hostile Mestalla venue, the Valencian players tried to thwart José Mourinho’s men by multiplying duels and provocations. Jude Bellingham notably found himself at the heart of several heated exchanges with Pepelu and Pablo Maffeo, even forcing Federico Valverde to intervene to calm his teammate. But it was when returning to the locker room after the break that the situation really degenerated. According to information revealed by A Punt Esportsthen detailed by ABC And Marcaa violent altercation broke out in the Mestalla tunnel, involving several Madrid players and members of security.

It all started with the protests of Braulio Vázquez, Valencia’s sporting director, who was particularly upset with the refereeing, particularly after a foul preceding Madrid’s first goal. “It’s not a foul, it’s not a foul!” Amazing ! »he would have repeated vehemently to one of the assistants. An attitude which required the intervention of the Spanish national police, as specified in the official report of the referee. But according to MarcaJude Bellingham then intervened by grabbing the Valencian leader’s suit to pull him away from the official, causing a new rise in tension. Several players from both teams then found themselves at the heart of a scuffle, forcing three security agents to intervene to try to separate the protagonists and push the Madrilenians back to their locker room.

And the accusations are particularly serious. According to the first revelations of the journalist Nacho Sanchis, of the À Punt channel, Jude Bellingham would have hit a security agent, while Antonio Rüdiger would have slapped another member of the system responsible for calming the spirits. Information also reported by ABC, which mentions the presence of Éder Militão at the time of the incidents. For its part, Marca provides latest details on the progress of this altercation. The Spanish daily claims that Rüdiger allegedly punched an agent in the face while the latter was trying to separate the players. Ibrahima Konaté also allegedly tried to calm the situation by repeatedly asking the protagonists to calm down. According to the Madrid media, Valencia even has video images showing the incidents, in particular the gesture of the German defender. Accusations that could place the two Real Madrid players in a delicate situation.

But one element is particularly noteworthy in Spain: the absence of these incidents in the referee’s official report. Although informed by the security agents, José Francisco Hernández Maeso did not mention any altercation involving the Madrid players. Only Braulio Vázquez appears in the report, the Valencian sporting director having had to be restrained and removed by security after his protests. A situation that Valencia CF does not understand, especially since the club has video evidence of the scuffle. Despite Real Madrid’s victory (3-0), this evening at Mestalla could therefore leave its mark. It remains to be seen whether the images evoked by the Spanish press will give rise to an examination by the disciplinary authorities and possible sanctions against the players concerned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Premier League managers are constantly in the spotlight but once they leave their role, sometimes they disappear very quickly into the background.

Plenty of Premier League managers have been on the back pages and appearing on Match of the Day one minute, only to become the answer to an obscure quiz question the next year.

Here are seven former Premier League managers who we have heard little to nothing about since they left the league.

It’s one of the more surprising names on this list considering how well he did with Huddersfield.

He took the completely unfancied Terriers up to the Premier League and even managed to keep them up, making it one of the best survival stories in the Premier League era.

The team naturally fell apart in the second season with Wagner relieved of his duties in January 2019 but his successive managerial stints have not come close to matching his time in Yorkshire.

Recent findings suggest that he all but took Schalke down and then ignored interest from West Brom to sign with Young Boys. He finished second with the serial league winners before returning to England and joining Norwich.

The German reached the playoffs with the Canaries but was hammered 4-0 and fresh sporting director Ben Knapper handed him the sack.

That was in 2024 but Wagner has been away from the touchline ever since.

He was linked with the USMNT but these days he can be found in the boardroom of RB Leipzig as the Academy Manager.

Unsurprisingly, winning zero Premier League games and failing to score in your four attempts is likely to put an end to your future hopes of managing in the league.

Frank de Boer is one of the worst Premier League managers in history according to the stats and his career post-Selhurst Park has failed to rebuild his reputation.

According to recent reports, he moved to Atlanta in the MLS and did actually do well, winning two cups in his first and finishing second. He got the boot in 2020 though he fell upwards to the role of Netherlands head coach.

A round of 16 loss to the Czech Republic at Euro 2020 was enough for De Boer to be sacked and his most recent job came in the UAE at Al Jazira. He could only get them to seventh though and was sacked midway through his first season.

Ever since, he has been away from the touchline except in a capacity as an analyst for Dutch TV channel ViaPlay.

Jose Mourinho’s long-time assistant went solo in 2013 as he took over Middlesbrough.

He got them up in 2016 but was always quite combustible and even started having a go at the club’s own fans for not cheering loud enough. That was the beginning of the end and he was sacked in March having fallen out with seemingly everyone at the club.

Recent findings suggest that karanka next joined Nottingham Forest but lost more games than he won and was given the sack a year later. His final appointment in England was at Birmingham, where he lost more than double the games he won.

Next he headed for Spain and Granada where he finally managed to have a positive record but not enough to keep his job and his most recent gig was four months spent as Maccabi Tel Aviv boss in 2023.

Now, he works as the technical director of development for the Spanish football federation, a role he has had since July 2025.

Recent findings suggest that long-time Fergie number two Phelan went out on his own as he took over Hull as caretaker, who had just gone up thanks to Steve Bruce. The fact that Bruce opted to resign rather than manage in the Premier League showed how significant a task awaited Phelan at Hull, who at that time insisted on being called Hull City Tigers.

With a very bare squad, Phelan somehow won games against Leicester and Swansea and even picked up the Premier League Manager of the Month gong for August.

That got him the job on a permanent basis but he was sacked in January as the club slid towards relegation.

After that he went to America for a brief stint as sporting director at Central Coast Mariners but he returned to Old Trafford as coach alongside Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

Recent findings suggest that when the Norwegian departed in December 2021, Phelan stayed on before three years later he followed Wayne Rooney to Plymouth Argyle to help his former player. Rooney was sacked shortly after and that ended Phelan’s time in management.

Instead, he set up his own company called Mike Phelan Coaching which provides support to grassroots clubs.

Sources indicate that the cards were stacked against Bradley when he arrived in the Premier League. He was the first American to manage in the league and was unfortunately very American.

His Latest Jersey accent rubbed plenty the wrong way, not least the Swansea Supporters’ Trust who owned almost a quarter of the club, and he was seen only getting the job because the club’s owners were American. His performance didn’t exactly quell that opinion.

He lost seven of his 11 games in charge before the Swansea board had to admit their mistake and sacked him the day after Boxing Day.

He left England and returned stateside where he spent 142 games in charge of LAFC. After that, he moved to Toronto but his most recent managerial stint was at Stabaek, a Norwegian side who he had managed previously.

That came to an end in 2024 and he has been out of the managerial game since. He also has gone down the punditry route and was an analyst for FOX Sports during the World Cup.

He was quite forgettable even at the time so perhaps we should not be surprised that former Swansea boss Guidolin has slipped even further from the public eye.

To be honest, we are surprised he is not Palermo manager, having been head coach there on four separate occasions.

Sacked on his 61st birthday, Guidolin left management after Swansea and is instead doing punditry and commentary work for DAZN in Italy.

Hasenhuttl’s work at Southampton (excluding the two 9-0s) felt like the start of a long career in England but not only has he been away from the country for four years, he hasn’t had a job in the last 12 months.

Following his departure from the Saints, he joined Bundesliga strugglers Wolfsburg, saving them from relegation.

He kept them clear of relegation troubles for the beginning of his first full campaign in charge but eight matches without a win, the last of which was a 4-0 defeat to Borussia Dortmund, spooked the board and he was sacked.

As for what he has been doing since, your guess is as good as ours. Not much has been heard of Hasenhuttl since his Wolfsburg departure. It would seem likely that at 59, he still fancies working in management but he has been waiting a while now.

My Everton #179: Loyalty & Love From Namibia

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Evertonfc

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My love for Everton began when I was just eight years old.
  • At that age, football was more than just a game to me; it was something that brought me happiness, excitement and dreams.
  • Recent findings suggest that wayne Rooney was my favourite player and my biggest inspiration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My love for Everton began when I was just eight years old.

At that age, football was more than just a game to me; it was something that brought me happiness, excitement and dreams.

Recent findings suggest that wayne Rooney was my favourite player and my biggest inspiration. He was not just a footballer I admired; he was someone I looked up to. In fact, when we played football in my village, my friends would call me "Rooney" because of how much I admired him and wanted to play like him.

Industry observers note that when Rooney eventually moved to Manchester United, I found myself facing a difficult decision. Naturally, I wanted to follow him because he was my role model.

I thought about becoming a Manchester United supporter, but something inside me would not allow it. No matter how much I admired Rooney, my heart still belonged to Everton.

It has been revealed that I realised my connection with the Club was much deeper than supporting a single player. It was a love that had already taken root in my heart.

Sources indicate that then came another special moment in my Everton journey. When Jordan Pickford joined the club in 2017, I was also transitioning into playing as a goalkeeper.

Watching him defend the goal inspired me in a latest way. I saw in him someone I could learn from, someone who motivated me to become a better goalkeeper and strengthened my love for Everton.

From that moment, I became even more certain that Everton was my club, and I was proud to call myself a true Evertonian.

Being an Everton supporter in Namibia is not always easy.

According to recent reports, we are few, and sometimes it feels like we are a rare breed. As far as I know, I have only met two other Everton supporters here, including my girlfriend, who is also an Evertonian.

Most of my friends often ask: "Bro, why do you support Everton?".

But my answer has always been simple: I support Everton because my love for this club is all about loyalty, passion, and the memories that have shaped who I am.

It has been revealed that for me, Everton is more than just a football club. It is part of my childhood, part of my identity, and part of my story. From an eight-year-old boy who admired Wayne Rooney to the young man I am today, my love for this club has remained unchanged.

Every match, every goal, every victory, and even every heartbreak has added another chapter to my journey as an Evertonian.

I may be thousands of kilometres away, but my heart has always been with Everton.

Geography cannot weaken a love that has lasted for more than a decade, and difficult seasons cannot erase the memories that made me fall in love with this beautiful club.

I am proud to be an Evertonian.

I was there in the good times, I've been here in the difficult times and I will be here when the glory returns. Because once Everton gets into your heart, it never truly leaves.

My Everton shares first-hand accounts describing the most-treasured memories of fans, players, and staff both past and present.

#13915. Breaking: Nani, Man Utd, and the unfair portrayal of a ‘frustrating’ talent

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1222 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Planetfootball ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Nani, Man Utd, and the unfair portrayal of a ‘frustrating’ talent

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1222 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Throughout the majority of his playing career, former Manchester United winger Nani has been called ‘frustrating’.
  • According to recent reports, life can be frustrating.
  • In an interview with Ball Street in 2017, former Manchester United and England defender Rio Ferdinand got some personal frustration off his chest, talking about one particular bugbear from his time at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Throughout the majority of his playing career, former Manchester United winger Nani has been called ‘frustrating’. Why not just enjoy the show?

According to recent reports, life can be frustrating. Hangnails. Queues. Taxes. These things aren’t the end of the world, but all of them, despite their smallness, can frustrate.

In an interview with Ball Street in 2017, former Manchester United and England defender Rio Ferdinand got some personal frustration off his chest, talking about one particular bugbear from his time at Old Trafford.

“I think the most frustrating thing,” he noted, “is when you know you’ve got players in your team with undoubted ability — great ability, got everything — but don’t consistently get that out onto the pitch.”.

The object of that frustration was Nani, a team-mate of Ferdinand’s for seven years.

Industry observers note that according to Ferdinand, Nani simply never learned to control his talents. What happened in training, mesmerising skills and thumping shots, was only occasionally replicated on match-day, and the winger, for the most part, simply didn’t live up to his potential.

Industry observers note that ferdinand wasn’t alone in holding this opinion. A cursory search for ‘frustrating Nani’ brings up countless results, with everybody from football journalists to other ex-United players chiming in with similar words.

Recent findings suggest that nani has to be one of the most frustrating players around. So much natural ability but you just don't know what your going to get from him.

— Danny Higginbotham (@Higginbotham05) June 16, 2014.

https://twitter.com/grahamruthven/status/741671670453264384.

Also a big evening for nani playing against Chelsea. Such a frustrating player. Immense ability but so inconsistent.

— Danny Higginbotham (@Higginbotham05) September 30, 2014.

In what was probably the most extreme case of Nani frustration, former United academy player Danny Higginbotham actually came to the same conclusion twice in the space of three months.

It has been revealed that the frustrated have some justification for their annoyance. Nani’s talent was – and still is – evident, but during his spell in England, people saw that talent as being regularly misused — expended on needless tricks, ambitious long-range shots and generally poor decision making.

That ability to frustrate was increased by a frequent proximity to Cristiano Ronaldo, a player who would prove impossible to replace at Mancheter United and who, funnily enough, once got incredibly frustrated with his younger compatriot.

When Nani ruined one of Ronaldo's greatest goals for Portugal 😂 pic.twitter.com/aUPE4bzu5I.

— Mark O'Haire (@MarkOHaire) April 15, 2020.

For three specific reasons, however, I believe it is impossible for a football fan to consider Nani a frustration, a disappointment or anything less than the genius that he is.

When Manchester United and Chelsea contested the 2008 Champions League Final, the match went to a penalty shootout.

In a recent development, after eight kicks, and with Cristiano Ronaldo’s miss separating the scores, the spotlight turned to the teams’ respective fifth-in-line takers. The deciders. The key men.

For United, the responsibility was handed to 21-year-old Nani, playing in the final match of his debut season; for Chelsea, it was 27-year-old captain John Terry.

For Nani’s side to have any chance of winning the game, the young winger needed to score and hope that Terry did not.

The coincidental pairing of Nani and Terry back in 2008 is interesting, because if anybody knows what ‘frustration’ is, it’s surely the man who has just fallen on his arse in front of 70,000 people at the most crucial moment of his career.

That just has to be frustrating.

For the fans, too: if seeing a player on your team attempt one too many step-overs can be frustrating, then seeing your captain — an ostensibly non-frustrating player — fail where the chief frustrater has just calmly succeeded must be the epitome of frustration.

Less than a year into his Manchester United career, Nani stepped up ahead of senior players like Ryan Giggs and — appropriately — Rio Ferdinand, converting a critical penalty against a world-class goalkeeper.

For that, he earned the right to attempt an infinite number of step-overs.

﻿.

Nani has defied his critics on several other occasions.

In February 2008, a few months before that penalty against Chelsea, the winger provided some curious quotes to the Daily Mail.

“In Portugal I have done this many times, but it is only because it is an entertaining spectacle and not because I disrespect my rivals,” he mentioned.

“I am a professional and am always very respectful with all the opposing players, but I do appreciate now that it may have looked bad.”.

In truth, what Nani had just done — the grave action for which he was publicly apologising — actually looked pretty good.

With Manchester United 4-0 up in an FA Cup tie against Arsenal, the Portuguese attacker pulled off a frankly hilarious series of keep-ups — knee, head, head, head, knee, knee, foot — to shield the ball from a furious (and, in all honesty, frustrated) William Gallas.

“Professionals don’t like that, when players turn on a bit of circus stuff,” explained John Motson just seconds after chuckling at the events unfolding in front of him.

﻿.

Nani’s infamous seal dribble may not have won his team the FA Cup, but it was anything but frustrating.

Sources indicate that frustration is having to get up at 6am, catch the bus and work a rubbish job. Football, as Nani well knows, should be a release from that frustration.

If John Terry and William Gallas falling over for various reasons isn’t enough to convince fans of Nani’s value, then perhaps the winger’s trophies are.

The most important of the bunch came two years ago, when the former Man United player took the captain’s armband from the injured Cristiano Ronaldo — the player he was, in the eyes of many demanding observers, supposed to emulate — in the final of Euro 2016.

Charged with the responsibility of leading his team, Nani helped Portugal to their first ever European Championship.

“It was a very strange feeling when Cristiano went off because I was very upset about losing our captain and our best player,” Nani told The Guardian a month after the tournament.

“But very promptly I had to put my head up and try to help the team, try to give them the confidence and motivation to continue. I had to do my job. I had to do what captains have to do.”.

The final at the Stade de France was frustrating — agonising, even — for the injured Ronaldo.

For the deputy captain, however, it was simply a matter of doing what he did best: dribble, cross, dribble, cross.

Many fans (and former team-mates) will still view Nani as one of the Premier League’s most frustrating players, but considering all the entertainment the player has provided over the years — the long-range screamers, the seal dribble, the backflip celebration — as well as the significant achievements that have accompanied those moments, you have to wonder if that frustration could be cured by just… lightening up a little.

In a recent development, football, as Nani has shown, can be fun. Let it be.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC.

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026.

Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

The Germany manager said Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter.

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager said.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion plan fell apart.

In a recent development, but he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his proposal. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

Would Wayne Rooney have worked in Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “I would have loved to play for Barcelona,” Wayne Rooney said recently.
  • Sources indicate that “Barça beat us in the Champions League final and they didn’t have a reference No.
  • Well, Wayne, let us be the judge of that as we picture a world where Rooney does indeed join Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“I would have loved to play for Barcelona,” Wayne Rooney said recently.

Sources indicate that “Barça beat us in the Champions League final and they didn’t have a reference No. 9. I think it would have been easy to play in that team, I would’ve fitted in perfectly.”.

Well, Wayne, let us be the judge of that as we picture a world where Rooney does indeed join Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona team.

First, let’s discuss the kind of player he was.

Terrifyingly for the rest of us, there will be some football watchers who now know Rooney as a manager or a pundit more than they did as a player, so let us fill you in on what he was like on the pitch.

Industry observers note that simply put, Rooney was one of the best young talents ever seen in football. There were non-ridiculous comparisons between him, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.

Rooney never finished in the top three of the Ballon d’Or for his entire career, which seems mental to even think about, but if you would have asked anyone from 2005 to 2010, who the best player in the world was, he would have got a mention.

Sources indicate that what made Rooney excellent was that he in a lot of ways a typical English striker. He is only 5ft 10’ so shorter than your average centre forward but what he lacked in going upwards, he made up for in going through.

It has been revealed that rooney weighed around 80kg during his United days. As a comparison, Eli Junior Kroupi is the same height and weighs 70kg. Yoane Wissa, also of a similar height, weighs 74kg.

But it was not fat that pushed Rooney up to the higher weight, it was muscle. Rio Ferdinand stated Rooney had a “caveman” strength from a very young age. There are reports he was able to bench press 110 kg as a 15-year-old.

According to recent reports, rooney’s physicality was a nightmare for defenders to play against. We can all remember him for the reckless challenges and flying slide tackles but for every one of those, there are 20 examples of him muscling free of a defender.

A number nine who is strong isn’t groundbreaking but what separated Rooney from the pack was that he had the physicality but combined it with a technical ability rarely seen in an English centre forward.

It was his most continental ability and one that was there from very early on. Look at this goal for Everton against Arsenal, the one that had commentator Clive Tyldesley telling everyone to remember the name.

The experienced Sol Campbell gives Rooney plenty of space on the edge, for the logical reasons that this is a 16-year-old who does probably not have the confidence to be trying those kinds of shots and you would have to be a pretty good player to beat David Seaman from that range.

According to recent reports, given that space, Rooney looks up then picks his spot. He sidefoots it, giving it the curl needed to go up and down in the short space of time. Seaman is at full stretch and doesn’t get close to it. It kisses the bar on the way in one of the most perfectly hit shots in Premier League history.

There are countless examples of Rooney displaying the kind of technical superiority ahead of players in the league.

It was not just shooting too, Rooney was one of the best passers in the league too. His chip to Robin Van Persie in 2013 was hit hard enough to travel 40 yards in no time at all but with a delicacy that allowed it to slow and drop perfect for Van Persie, meaning the Dutchman did not have to break his stride before volleying it in.

Rooney’s ability was not lost on other players either. In 2015, he received this compliment from Xavi: “Wayne Rooney is a player I have admired for a long time. He is an extraordinary player with extraordinary capabilities.”.

As well as the strength and technical ability Rooney had, he combined that with a relentlessness. Rooney grew up boxing in Merseyside, he is the footballing version of Rocky Balboa. And what that gave him was an incredible work rate. What he lacked in diet discipline over the summer, he made up in running hard yards during games, something he now laments the current United squad for failing to do.

That desire comes with a lot of positives, not least it gets the crowd on your side, but there are negatives too, such as being dragged out of position in search of the ball but also Rooney had a rawness and rashness when it came to challenges. Four club career red cards feels on the low side.

Recent findings suggest that put it all together and you have a physical, relentless player who also has the technique to play at the highest of levels. Now what about Barcelona?

The forgotten story of… Wayne Rooney’s Man Utd transfer request in 2010.

The tactical philosophy of Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona has been well studied and adopted all over the world to varying degrees of success.

It was most effective at Barcelona due to being relatively in its infancy and also Guardiola was blessed with infinite talents who had been developed to play this exact style of football.

Industry observers note that it resulted in two Champions Leagues, three league titles and the first ever sextuple. But what was it exactly?

The best example of it came in that Wembley final, when Barcelona picked apart Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United.

According to recent reports, tiki-taka, as it came to be known, was an evolution on the foundations laid by Johan Cruyff. It can rather falsely be labelled as pass, pass, pass but every pass in a perfect Guardiola system is with a purpose. The idea is to pull your opponent into areas they don’t want to be so that their team becomes streched, opening gaps. Being a Barcelona player is as much about running off the ball to create space for your teammate as it is what you do on it.

It has been revealed that for players to succeed in Pep’s system, they need the combination of great passing ability, the technical quality to swiftly control the ball and release and the spatial awareness to create space for their teammates via their positioning. They also need to run an awful lot.

Sources indicate that as for what Guardiola wanted from his number nine, he very rarely played with a traditional number nine. He tried it with Zlatan Ibrahimovic and it famously did not work, although they may just as much to do with his Swedish attitude as it is with his ability.

Typically though, Guardiola wanted a number nine who could drop deep and overload the midfield. Guardiola loves his teams to exploit the half spaces between defensive lines and by having a false nine, he could operate in the area too far forward for the centre backs and too deep for the midfielders.

So the profile of player we are looking for is a technically excellent, intelligent player who can operate just as well in a 10 as he can as a nine. And that sounds a lot like Wayne Rooney.

According to recent reports, as Rooney revealed in his late career once his speed gave way, he is able to drop deep and essentially play as an advanced midfielder. At Barcelona, his move to that position may have been expedited by Guardiola’s desire to have him play as a false nine.

It has been revealed that rooney’s physicality would also add something new to a largely unphysical Barcelona front line. At the time they had Messi, Pedro and David Villa, three players you would not describe as overly physical, even if Messi in particular is far stronger than he often gets credited for.

There is every reason to think that Rooney would actually work very well in a Barcelona system, the only problem is one that Ibrahimovic also ran into – Messi.

Sources indicate that for that Wembley final, Guardiola deployed Messi in the number nine spot which is where he played for the majority of the season. It was a new tactic by Guardiola as in the previous season, Messi played 39 matches on the right side compared to 12 in the centre forward position.

In 2010/11, those numbers flipped with Messi playing 43 times through the middle compared to 11 on the wing. In those 43 games, Messi scored 46 goals.

In their ideal worlds, Messi and Rooney would likely have wanted to operate in similar areas of the pitch and there would only be one winner in a potential battle for supremacy.

In a recent development, so while Rooney would have worked in Guardiola’s Barcelona, he would have arguably been even more impactful in Luis Enrique’s Barcelona. By the time Enrique took over, Barcelona had become much more direct and played Luis Suarez as a typical nine who could bring both Messi and Neymar into play.

Put Rooney into that system and it would have been scary.

Overall, it is fair to say that a player as technically gifted as Rooney would have definitely worked at Barcelona but he would have found himself in the shadow of Messi as so many other great players did. Still, he probably would have had a lot of trophies to help him get over that fact.

#13898. Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (418 w)

Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (418 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

Coming off the back of a 6-0 victory at Goodison last night, Scott Phelan's Blues head into this weekend’s clash against Spurs with a four-game unbeaten streak and unrivalled confidence.

In a recent development, on last night’s cup match against Durham, the head coach highlighted the squad’s “top of their game” performance. Everton dominated possession for the full 90 minutes of the game, using additional "time on the ball" to net six goals – with a hattrick from Japanese forward Yuka Momiki.

Phelan now hopes that the team can gain momentum from the impressive victory.

"Last night was an opportunity to show the top of our game and have a lot of the ball," said Phelan in his pre-match press conference on Thursday afternoon. "That will hopefully give the players a confidence boost.".

On the WSL season so far, Phelan commended the players' “excellent” performance in a series of “challenging” fixtures. The last two weekends seeing the Blues hold a strong fort against high-flying Manchester United and Chelsea, bringing both matches to a draw.

Recent findings suggest that "It has been a positive last three fixtures," he continued. "We knew this run of fixtures would be challenging, but to see the players performing has been excellent.

The 2026/27 season has also seen the introduction of the Subway Players Cup. An excited Phelan maintains that this is a “positive addition” to the league, as “more games and opportunities” are available to players.

Sources indicate that "It enhances the league so there's more games and more opportunities. Overall. it has been a positive addition.

The overall strong form of the team has seen them progress further in the league, with the former Under-21s captain noting that this was one of the “challenges” they were up against this season.

"Four games, four wins," he stated. "That gives us a real strong chance of progressing which was one of the challenges for this season.

Saturday’s game sees Everton face Spurs away from home, with no fresh injuries in the squad heading into this weekend.

Recovering centre-back Megan Finnigan started in Wednesday’s cup match, with Phelan saying he is "pleased to see her getting 90 minutes on the pitch after a long time injured.".

It has been revealed that last season saw Everton beat the Londoners 2-1 away from home. The Blues’ head coach is confident that his squad can bring fierce competition and good form into this weekend’s reunion.

Rio Ngumoha dazzles on coming-of-age night in Europe

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5313 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.
  • Industry observers note that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality.
  • Ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

Industry observers note that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

Ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

According to recent reports, iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola mentioned. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha remarked to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

Iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

The floodgates are opening ⚽️ Florian Wirtz scores his first goal of the season for Liverpool 🇩🇪 https://t.co/5HP72tA3bE.

Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

In a recent development, “We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he stated, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

A moment to forget for Virgil van Dijk 😨 Georges Mikautadze takes full advantage to give Villarreal the lead at Anfield 🟡⚽️ https://t.co/3JTl00UwYa.

According to recent reports, the pace of the game was slow and Villarreal were in control until the later stages of the half. Koumas and Cody Gakpo created a chance and from the corner that resulted Mac Allister headed in Tsimikas’s cross. Liverpool were up and running. Ngumoha’s cross from the left was unwisely left by Cardona for Araújo to score and the game was level.

Out of nowhere 😳 Ronald Araújo sneaks in to grab Liverpool's equaliser on the stroke of half-time 🇺🇾 https://t.co/Qrn8PmB2bJ.

Then came Ngumoha’s big second half, creating the third for Mac Allister. The teenager went past Cardona and the substitute Juan Foyth in a couple of strides. Wirtz dispatched the fourth from Gakpo’s ball.

Even so there was still time for Liverpool to show that they had sacrificed some defensive stability. The absence of a right-back cost them when substitute Tani Oluwaseyi ran into that area of the pitch to score Villarreal’s third late on. The third win of Liverpool’s Champions League season puts them second in the 36-team super-table, and behind defending champions Paris St-Germain only on goal difference.

Liverpool are also seeing a fresh star emerge. Ngumoha might be the most expensive academy signing in the game’s modern history but alongside the £100m men he looks like a risk that was worth taking.

We have said all night about momentum, and talking about how they Liverpool will play against Brighton at the weekend, I’ll be amazed if Rio [Ngumoha] doesn’t start because of the momentum that he has got from this game.

You see the fans, you see how everyone got a lift by him and that’s what they need at the weekend, they need someone to lift them.

Sources indicate that they are flying. Their confidence is through the roof. A similar style to Villarreal. They are second in everything after Barcelona. It has been a good game to prepare and we will use it.

Industry observers note that I am really happy with Rio. He is trying to improve everything and we are trying to correct things. He played a lot on the left and know he is playing a lot on the right and he has adapted really well. We encourage him always. Even defensively as well he is improving. He has become a more complete player – and we must not forget he is 18!

Rio Ngumoha was magnificent tonight. Such a threat, and he dedicated himself to his tasks. On the ball this kid has so much potential, and I say kid, but he’s a young man. He has so much quality and it’s stuff that you can’t teach to be honest.

In a recent development, what he does with the ball at his feet, that is God given ability, and his hard work on the training pitch, doing things day in and day out, and being ruthless, is what he mentioned in his interview, and I like that. He wants to be decisive, and I love that about him.

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

They have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

The records that Max Dowman has already broken – & the next he could smash with Arsenal and England

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Max Dowman is a little over a month away from his 17th birthday but he has already racked up an impressive number of records in football.
  • The Arsenal winger scored a late winner to give England U21s a 3-2 victory over France’s equivalent age group and in doing so, became the youngest scorer for England’s U21 age group.
  • That adds to a growing list of records the Arsenal man has already achieved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Dowman is a little over a month away from his 17th birthday but he has already racked up an impressive number of records in football.

The Arsenal winger scored a late winner to give England U21s a 3-2 victory over France’s equivalent age group and in doing so, became the youngest scorer for England’s U21 age group.

That adds to a growing list of records the Arsenal man has already achieved.

Youngest goalscorer in Premier League history.

While he missed out on the youngest player to feature in the Premier League by a couple of months to his Arsenal teammate Ethan Nwaneri, Dowman is at the moment the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history.

Dowman netted against Everton in March at the age of 16 years and 73 days, beating Everton’s James Vaughan to the record.

Vaughan scored back in April 2005 when he was 16 years and 270 days old. Other 16-year-olds to score in the top flight include James Milner, Wayne Rooney and Rio Ngumoha.

Youngest player to win the Premier League.

Dowman already has a Premier League winners medal and is the youngest to have ever lifted the trophy.

Dowman was 16 years and 144 days when Arsenal lifted the trophy away at Crystal Palace on the final day of last season and took the record off Manchester City’s Phil Foden.

The first title Foden was involved in was the 2017/18 season when Foden was 17 years and 350 days old.

Dowman also had a bigger role than Foden as he played six, scored one and assisted one compared to Foden’s one assist in five games.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis is third on the list having been 18 years and 188 days when City lifted the title in 2023.

Youngest player to appear in the UEFA Champions League.

Dowman also has history in Europe too after he became the youngest player to ever feature in the Champions League.

He was 15 years, 10 months and four days when he appeared in Arsenal’s 3-0 win over Slavia Prague last year, beating the former record set by Dortmund’s Youssoufa Moukoko in 2020.

England Under-21s youngest-ever player and goalscorer.

Dowman’s appearance in the 1-0 loss to Portugal earlier this month saw him become the youngest player to ever represent England at the U21 level, beating the previous record set by Jude Bellingham.

His goal against France added yet another record to his tally as he took another record away from Bellingham.

England’s next Ballon d’Or winner: Ranking the 5 favourites after Harry Kane’s historic triumph.

With hopefully a long career ahead of him, there are plenty of records Dowman could break.

Dowman has two more chances to become the youngest Champions League winner in history. That record at the moment belongs to Nwankwo Kanu who was 18 years and 296 days old when Ajax won it in 1995.

Sources indicate that should Arsenal reach the final this season in Madrid, Dowman will be 17 years and 149 days old. Should Arsenal fail this year, Dowman could win it at the age of 18 years and 148 days the following season.

Industry observers note that one record Dowman will not be able to achieve is becoming the youngest appearance maker in England history. This international break window was the final chance for Dowman to do it for he will be 17 years and 81 days by the time of the next one in March. Theo Walcott was 17 years and 75 days when he set the record back in 2006.

Given he started so young, Dowman has a good chance to break a lot of Arsenal records too.

The obvious one would be going after the record appearance holder. That at the moment belongs to David O’Leary who played 722 games from 1975 to 1993.

Dowman is just a tad short of that presently on 19 but say Arsenal play around 60 games a season and Dowman plays in every one of those, he would reach O’Leary in 12 seasons.

Obviously he is not going to play in every single match and so if we are a little more conservative, you could say he would reach that mark around 15/16 seasons from now, should he develop into a starter. 16 seasons from now would put him at 33 which is not over the hill for a footballer by any means.

If someone plays that amount of games, you would also fancy him to have a good chance of becoming Arsenal’s top scorer of all time. That accolade presently belongs to Thierry Henry who scored 228 in 377 games. Dowman is currently on three so plenty of ground to catch up.

Playing that many games will also likely see him come close to the top of the appearances makers in the Premier League. James Milner right now has that title, having played 658 games in the top division. Dowman is currently on eight.

  • Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.
